// A name declared inside the subtest closure is not automatically the
// testing.TB the closure was handed. `parent := held.tb` is a local
// declaration holding the enclosing test's TB, and the qt.New built from it
// reports its failures against the parent test exactly as `qt.New(held.tb)`
// does. Nothing else in the file gives it away: the closure's own parameter is
// never touched, and the enclosing-scope walk sees only `held`, which is
// neither a checker nor a testing.TB.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type fixtureTB struct {
	tb testing.TB
}

func TestCheckerFromALocalCopyOfAFieldTB(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the local name holds the parent's TB", func(t *testing.T) {
		parent := held.tb
		c := qt.New(parent)
		c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestCheckerFromALocalCopyTwoStepsOn(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the copy is one name further away", func(t *testing.T) {
		first := held.tb
		second := first
		c := qt.New(second)
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}

// The four local spellings that are the TB this closure was handed, and must
// stay silent: the parameter itself, a copy of it, a var with the type written
// out, and the parameter of a helper closure written inside the subtest.
func TestConformingLocalTBSources(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("the closure's own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)
	})

	t.Run("a copy of the closure's own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		own := t
		c := qt.New(own)
		c.Assert(4, qt.Equals, 4)
	})

	t.Run("a var whose type is written out", func(t *testing.T) {
		var own testing.TB = t
		c := qt.New(own)
		c.Assert(5, qt.Equals, 5)
	})

	t.Run("a helper closure builds from the TB it was handed", func(t *testing.T) {
		nested := func(tb testing.TB) {
			inner := qt.New(tb)
			inner.Assert(6, qt.Equals, 6)
		}
		nested(t)
	})
}
